editorial: When the front line becomes a newsroom, every headline edges closer to survival. Set in a near‑future America on the brink of civil war, the film pulls you into the claustrophobic world of war reporters who must navigate both truth and terror. The standout element is the film’s relentlessly handheld camera that keeps you anchored to the frantic rhythm of reportage, while a brutal soundscape amplifies the feeling that all systems are failing. Watchers will find the icy pace disconcerting at times, as the narrative takes longer than desired to personify its stakes. Still, if you crave a tense, introspective look at media and conflict, you’ll be gripped from the first frame.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of political thrillers who appreciate a slow-burn narrative.
